title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC found the complaint judicially out of order because the defendant’s objections belonged first in the ongoing original-jurisdiction process and, if unresolved, in a later appeal. It did not decide the objections on their merits.
first_summary: Thompson used a BCO 43 complaint to challenge his Session indictment during an ongoing disciplinary case. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order because a defendant must raise such objections during the original proceeding and, if dissatisfied, pursue them on appeal. It did not decide the indictment objection’s merits.
summary: Thompson used a BCO 43 complaint to challenge his Session indictment during an ongoing disciplinary case, according to the separate concurrence. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order. It held that a defendant must raise such objections during process in the court of original jurisdiction under BCO 32-14 and, if still dissatisfied, pursue them on appeal under BCO 42-3. The ruling did not decide the indictment objection’s merits.

sources.supports: Case identity, adopted disposition and rationale, adoption vote, and the concurrence’s description of the indictment challenge.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Caption and decision date appear at lines 13–17; the amended panel decision was adopted by the SJC at lines 26–30 (printed pages 514–515).
evidence_notes.dispute: The separate concurrence describes Thompson’s complaint as challenging the legitimacy of his Session indictment during pending process, lines 38–46 (printed page 515).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The adopted ruling finds the complaint judicially out of order and directs that objections be raised during original-jurisdiction process or later appeal, lines 19–22 (printed page 514).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The indictment details and irreparable-harm discussion come from a separate concurrence, not the adopted rationale, lines 32–46 and 89–100 (printed pages 515, 517).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The concurrence analogizes Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery at lines 48–54; it is not incorporated as the operative judgment. The later Case 2015-11 result is mentioned only at line 122.

source_limits: The adopted decision is brief. Most factual background and additional interlocutory-review analysis appear only in the separate concurrence; the reproduced Marshall quotation is incomplete but unnecessary to determine this case’s disposition.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the attempted pretrial complaint concerning the Session indictment.

score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains that objections belong in the original process and then an appeal.
